quotes.text: ADAMS, JOHN, BIRTHPLACE HABS NO. MA-596 SECONDARY OR COMMON NAMES OF STRUCTURE COMPLETE ADDRESS (DESCRIBE LOCATION FOR RURAL SfTES) 133 Franklin Street DATE OF CONSTRUCTION (INCLUDE SOURCE) Ca. 1681, with later additions
ectangular main house, with lean-to and porch addition. Measures 41'-8" X 42'-5".
quotes.page: HABS Architectural Data Form, page 1, 'Shape and dimensions of structure'; the leading letter is cut off in the scan

quotes.text: nogging and clay mortar. The brick and mortar were removed during the 1897 restoration. The walls are constructed with wood studs. The house is covered with clapboards painted red. The house has a purlin system roof, which was raised on the north elevation to accommodate the lean-to and altered further by a gabled addition off the lean-to. The earlier gabled portion is still intact.
quotes.page: ADAMS, JOHN, BIRTHPLACE HABS No. MA-956 (page 2) -- as the running head prints it

quotes.text: The main stair is a winder type. The lean- to attic features the remains of two stairways to the first floor, but both have been closed.off.
quotes.page: HABS Architectural Data Form, page 1, 'Interior features of note'

quotes.text: The front frontispiece features a pedimented and pilastered surround. Some original roof sheathing is visible..The present sheathing is asphalt. White fascia boards flank gable slope.
quotes.page: HABS Architectural Data Form, page 1, 'Exterior features of note'
